forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. No publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session with named principals occurred before EOD June 16. The Islamabad MoU was signed remotely on June 17 — one calendar day past the horizon — with Trump at Versailles and Pezeshkian in Tehran; the first structured session convened June 21 at Burgenstock, Switzerland. Back-channel contact preceded June 17, but no session with named principals meeting the resolution criteria occurred before EOD June 16. RESIDUAL AMBIGUITY NOTED (dissent risk: HIGH): the June 14-15 virtual co-signing could be read as Iran 'officially rescinds the June 1 suspension.' Under the ambiguity rule, a virtual signing is closer to a 'written-message exchange at senior level' than a 'convened session'; no explicit Iranian MFA statement rescinding the suspension was issued. Ambiguity rule settles this as NO. Dissent documented in resolution record.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The 25th Knesset dissolved July 17 by a 62-0 vote — with all coalition partners voting for dissolution — completing the full four-year term, the first time since 1988. This was a normal term-end dissolution, not an early collapse. The 62-0 vote confirms the coalition retained its majority (opposition boycotted rather than voted against). The election date set is October 27, which is the scheduled term-end election date — not an 'earlier than Oct 27' date. Neither YES criterion was met: no majority loss occurred, and no early dissolution occurred. The question's YES criteria (majority loss or early dissolution moving date earlier than Oct 27) are definitively foreclosed. STRUCTURAL OBE NOTE: there is now no sitting Knesset in which the coalition could lose a majority before Oct 27; this structural fact makes any continued ACTIVE status moot. Weekly cadence violation also noted (40 days stale from last_reasoned_at of 2026-05-19). Replacement forecast for post-election coalition formation should be created as a fresh forecast once N5 resolves.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will the 7-day rolling average of commercial vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz reach 30 or more per day before EOD 2026-09-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Analyst proposed p=0.37; Judge reduces to p=0.28. Current transit level ~10/day July 19-20, down from post-MoU peak ~43 July 3. Pre-war baseline 120-140/day; 30/day = ~21-25% of normal. June 17 MoU brought recovery from near-zero to ~43 in ~16 days; Iran's renewed attacks after July 7 reversed this within days. A second ceasefire (N2, p=0.18) is necessary but not sufficient; MCM operations must resume; major shippers require sustained confidence. DA recommendation: reduce Hormuz recovery forecasts targeting ≥30 transits before August 10 to max 10%; N6's Sept 15 horizon extends beyond August 10 but the DA's logic applies to the early portion. Mechanical derivation: P(restored by Aug 10) ≤ 0.10; P(restored Aug 11-Sept 15 | not by Aug 10) ≈ P(late ceasefire cycle) × P(rapid recovery) ≈ 0.18 × 0.90 = 0.162; total P(N6) ≈ 0.10 + 0.90 × 0.162 ≈ 0.25. Judge sets p=0.28 (slightly above mechanical derivation to account for EIA-reported 8.5 million bbl/day military-escorted throughput providing a floor for rapid commercial recovery if political conditions change). CONFLICTING DATA NOTE: EIA reports 8.5 million bbl/day via military escort versus ~10 AIS-tracked commercial transits; this conflict adds uncertainty but the trend is toward continued closure, not recovery.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if an authoritative shipping data source reports a 7-day rolling average of ≥30 confirmed commercial vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz on any day before EOD Sept 15. Excludes warships and military support vessels but includes LNG, crude, and container ships with military escort.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: PortWatch (IMF), USNI News, Lloyd's List Intelligence, or MarineTraffic official data products. TIER1 news citing these sources with specific count data is acceptable.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If AIS data is systematically disrupted (transponders off for security) and counts are unreliable: hold resolution up to 7 days past horizon; if no clear data, resolve AMBIGUOUS. If 7-day average reaches 30 during a brief window before Iranian interdiction resumes, resolve YES if the 30 threshold was met on any single calculation date.
